items.title: DRC Ebola outbreak tops 900 cases as violence hampers response

featured_image.name: Ebola patients flee in attacks on Congo health facilities, hobbling response

items.description: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 900 suspected cases, with WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warning that the fast-moving epidemic is outrunning containment efforts. The Congolese government reported 904 suspected cases and 119 suspected fatalities as of Sunday, May 24, while attacks on health facilities have driven patients into communities and complicated an already strained response.[1][2]

items.title: AI safety filters on Meta, Google models stripped in minutes, FT finds

featured_image.name: Meta to start labeling AI-generated images from companies like OpenAI,  Google - iTnews

items.description: Software tools that remove safety protections from AI models developed by Meta and Google can bypass guardrails in a matter of minutes, according to an investigation published by the Financial Times on Sunday. The modified systems responded to prompts involving biological weapons, malware creation, and child exploitation, raising fresh concerns about the adequacy of voluntary safety measures across the AI industry.

items.title: WHO chief warns Ebola 'outpacing' response as deaths hit 220

featured_image.name: WHO emergency committee meets to discuss Congo Ebola outbreak

items.description:
The World Health Organization's director-general warned on Monday that the Ebola outbreak tearing through the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda is outrunning international containment efforts, with 220 suspected deaths and cases mounting rapidly across the region.

"We are urgently scaling up operations, but at the moment the epidemic is outpacing us," Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said, adding that a delay in detecting cases meant responders were now "playing catch-up." He said he would travel to Congo on Tuesday to assess the response firsthand.[1][2]

The remarks came as Uganda confirmed two additional Ebola cases on Monday, bringing its total to seven confirmed infections. The DRC remains the epicenter of the outbreak, with its health ministry reporting hundreds of suspected cases and deaths concentrated in the conflict-ridden Ituri and North Kivu provinces.[1]

items.title: Trump urges Arab leaders to normalize Israel ties as Iran deal nears

featured_image.name: Trump pushes Arab, Muslim leaders on Israel ties

items.description:
President Donald Trump told the leaders of several Arab and Muslim-majority countries during a phone call on Saturday that he expects them to normalize relations with Israel and join the Abraham Accords once a deal to end the war with Iran is reached, according to Axios. The request was reportedly met with silence from the leaders on the call, the Times of Israel reported.[1][2][3]

The call came as Washington and Tehran appeared close to signing a memorandum of understanding to end hostilities, with a senior U.S. official saying the deal could come "in the coming days". Trump declared Saturday that the agreement had been "largely negotiated," though disputes over wording, sanctions relief, frozen assets, and the terms of uranium disposal remain unresolved.[4][5][6]

items.title: Oil and LNG tankers resume Strait of Hormuz transits after three-month halt

featured_image.name: Japanese-affiliated LNG tanker sails through Strait of Hormuz

items.description: Multiple vessels carrying crude oil and liquefied natural gas have begun transiting the Strait of Hormuz, offering the clearest sign yet that limited commercial shipping is restarting after nearly three months of disruption caused by the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.

items.title: Inaudible sounds hidden in podcasts can hijack AI voice assistants, researchers find

featured_image.name: Researchers discover vulnerabilities in smart assistants' voice commands |  Malwarebytes Labs

items.description: A team of security researchers has shown that imperceptible audio signals hidden in podcasts, YouTube videos, and voice calls can manipulate AI voice assistants into performing unauthorized actions — a finding presented this week at the IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy in San Francisco that exposes a new class of vulnerability in the rapidly expanding world of voice-based AI.

items.title: Pope Leo XIV calls to 'disarm' AI in first encyclical

featured_image.name: VATICAN-ENCYCLICAL-MAGNIFICA HUMANITAS-AI-POPE

items.description:
Pope Leo XIV on Monday released his first encyclical, a sweeping nearly 43,000-word document that calls for the "disarming" of artificial intelligence and warns that the technology risks becoming a modern Tower of Babel if left unchecked in the hands of powerful corporations and governments.[1][2]

The encyclical, titled "Magnifica Humanitas" ("Magnificent Humanity"), was presented by the American-born pontiff in the Vatican's Synod Hall — a break with tradition, as popes do not typically speak at the launch of their own encyclicals. Joining him on the panel was Christopher Olah, co-founder of Anthropic, the AI safety company currently embroiled in a legal battle with the Trump administration over the military use of its technology.[3][4]

items.title: Iran says US deal 'not imminent' as both sides temper expectations

featured_image.name: Iran and US agree on 'guiding principles' for a deal, say Iranian officials

items.description:
Efforts to finalize a peace agreement between the United States and Iran slowed on Monday as both sides tempered expectations, with Iran's foreign ministry declaring that a deal is "not imminent" even as Secretary of State Marco Rubio suggested an announcement could come "maybe today."

The impasse centers on a proposed memorandum of understanding that would end the three-month-old war, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and set the stage for broader negotiations over Iran's nuclear program and sanctions relief. President Trump, posting on Truth Social over the weekend, said the deal "will either be a great and meaningful one, or there will be no deal," while cautioning his team not to "rush into" an agreement.[1][2]

items.title: Iran agreed to give up enriched uranium in US deal, officials say

featured_image.name: Top Iranian official says Tehran would forgo highly enriched uranium in nuclear  deal with Trump

items.description: Two US officials told the New York Times that Iran has agreed in broad terms to give up its stockpile of highly enriched uranium as part of a framework deal announced by President Donald Trump, who declared Saturday that a peace agreement had been "largely negotiated." But a senior Iranian source subsequently told Reuters that Tehran has not agreed to hand over its enriched uranium, highlighting the persistent contradictions between American and Iranian accounts of the deal's terms.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Trump says Iran deal 'largely negotiated,' Strait of Hormuz to reopen

featured_image.name: Trump gives Iran 48-hour deadline to reopen Strait of Hormuz or face new  strikes

items.description: President Donald Trump declared Saturday that a memorandum of understanding with Iran has been "largely negotiated," with final details to be announced shortly, marking the most concrete step yet toward ending months of conflict between the two nations.

items.title: Trump tells negotiators not to rush Iran deal

featured_image.name: LIVE: Trump instructs negotiators 'not to rush into a deal' with Iran

items.description:
President Donald Trump said on Sunday that he has instructed his negotiators not to "rush into a deal" with Iran, declaring that the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports will "remain in full force and effect" until a final agreement is "reached, certified, and signed."[1][2][3]

The statement came just a day after Trump posted on Truth Social that a memorandum of understanding to end the months-long conflict had been "largely negotiated," raising expectations for an imminent breakthrough.[3][4]

items.title: Iran agrees to surrender enriched uranium as US deal nears, officials say

featured_image.name: Iran Nuclear: Rising IAEA Inspections Can't Fix Deepening Mistrust -  Bloomberg

items.description: President Donald Trump announced Saturday that a peace agreement with Iran has been "largely negotiated," including the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global energy waterway that has been closed during the conflict between the two nations.

items.title: Ebola patients flee DRC facility after arson as cases near 800

featured_image.name: Ebola Patients Flee After Second Treatment Tent Set on Fire—'Panic'

items.description: The Ebola outbreak tearing through eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has grown to nearly 750 suspected cases and 177 suspected deaths, with the disease now spreading across borders into Uganda and prompting emergency declarations from global health authorities.

items.title: Russia fires Oreshnik missile in massive assault on Kyiv

featured_image.name: Russia launched Oreshnik missile at Kyiv Oblast in overnight attack ...

items.description:
Russia unleashed one of its most devastating aerial assaults on Kyiv since the full-scale invasion began, firing 90 missiles and 600 drones at the Ukrainian capital and surrounding areas overnight Sunday, killing at least four people and wounding more than 80, according to Ukrainian officials.[1][2]

Multiple rounds of explosions were heard across the city throughout the early morning hours in a bombardment that lasted more than five hours, damaging residential buildings, schools, markets, and a trade center across the capital.[3][4]

items.title: Zelensky calls Germany's associate EU membership plan 'unfair'

featured_image.name: Exclusive-Ukraine's Zelenskiy says proposal of associate EU ...

items.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told EU leaders in a letter sent late on Friday that a German proposal to grant Ukraine "associate" membership of the European Union was "unfair" because it would leave Kyiv without a voice inside the bloc, according to Reuters, which reviewed the message.[1][2]

"It would be unfair for Ukraine to be present in the European Union, but remain voiceless," Zelensky wrote. "The time is right to move forward with Ukraine's membership in a full and meaningful way."[2][1]

items.title: Taiwan says China deployed 100-plus vessels after Trump-Xi summit

featured_image.name: Chinese military exercises foreshadow a blockade of Taiwan

items.description: Taiwan's National Security Council chief Joseph Wu said Saturday that China has deployed more than 100 navy, coast guard, and other vessels across regional waters in what marks one of Beijing's largest maritime shows of force in recent memory, raising alarm over China's intentions toward the self-governing island.[1][2][3]

items.title: U.S. has 'almost completely excluded' Israel from Iran talks, officials say

featured_image.name: US has almost completely excluded Israel from negotiations with ...

items.description: The United States has "almost completely excluded" Israel from ongoing negotiations with Iran, Israeli defense officials told The New York Times this week, as a widening rift between President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu threatens to reshape Middle Eastern geopolitics.[1]

items.title: Zelensky confirms strike on chemical plant 1,700 km inside Russia

featured_image.name: Ukrainian drones strike Russian chemical giant's plant over 1,700  kilometers from front lines

items.description: Ukraine escalated its long-range drone campaign overnight on May 23, hitting an oil terminal in the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk and a chemical plant nearly 1,700 kilometers from the border, as Kyiv continues to target the energy and industrial infrastructure underpinning Russia's war machine.

items.title: Ukraine hits Russian frigate, oil terminals in Novorossiysk

featured_image.name: Frigate Admiral Essen of the Black Sea Fleet of the Russian Federation in  Sevastopol Bay

items.description: Ukrainian forces launched a multi-target overnight assault on the Russian Black Sea port of Novorossiysk on the night of May 22-23, hitting the frigate Admiral Essen, a missile hovercraft, and oil infrastructure, according to Ukrainian military sources and Russian officials.

items.title: US naval blockade of Iran hits 100 redirected ships

featured_image.name: CENTCOM boasts month-long Iran naval blockade, redirecting 67 commercial  ships

items.description:
U.S. Central Command announced on Friday that American forces have redirected more than 100 commercial vessels since the naval blockade of Iranian ports began on April 13, marking a milestone in the six-week-old maritime operation designed to choke off Tehran's oil exports.[1][2]

The achievement comes as CENTCOM steadily escalated its enforcement figures — from 37 ships redirected by April 25, to 58 by May 8, 67 by May 12, 85 by May 18, and 94 as of May 21 — underscoring the pace of commercial traffic still attempting to reach Iranian waters despite the blockade.[3][4][5][6][7]
